solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Protest of soldiers facing battle site beginning to retreat into base

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a regiment of soldiers
Mons in Belgium, scene of a 1914 battle; the setter's wordplay has one S too many, so only MON can be used here

indicators.note: into tells us the letter from retreat goes inside the word for base

parts.note: a station is a military base

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, so only the start of retreat is used

explanation.surface: Troops grumble about a front line where they are starting to fall back to camp.
explanation.walkthrough: Setter's slip: MONS (the Belgian battlefield) and STATION share one S the answer has once; Bradman admitted it on the blog. 'into' puts R inside STATION to make STRATION.
explanation.definitionFit: A remonstration is a forceful objection, so it is a synonym for a protest.

clue.text: In bumpy ride everyone pulled together

indicators.note: In places the word for everyone inside the jumbled letters
a bumpy ride is shaken about, so its letters are jumbled

parts.note: all means everyone

explanation.surface: On a rough journey the passengers all helped each other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bumpy' is the anagram signal and 'In' the insertion; 'everyone' is not the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To rally is to come together for a common effort, so the past tense is a synonym.

clue.text: After limbo dancing, side is loosened up, ready for action

indicators.note: dancing moves the letters of limbo around
loosened up suggests the letters of side are shaken free and rearranged

explanation.surface: A dancer, limber after doing the limbo, feels prepared to go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' rearranges LIMBO to MOBIL; 'loosened up' rearranges SIDE to ISED.
explanation.definitionFit: Mobilised troops have been prepared and deployed, so the word means made ready for action.

clue.text: Drug dealer participating in seminar complacently

indicators.note: participating in says the word takes part inside the run of letters that follows

explanation.surface: A drug trafficker sits smugly through a lecture.
explanation.definitionFit: Narco is slang, mainly American, for a trafficker in illegal drugs.

clue.text: Audible assessment of TV critic for a particular sort of turn

indicators.note: Audible says what follows is heard, not seen written

parts.note: a TV critic's assessment would be a telly mark, a score given to television

explanation.surface: A reviewer's spoken verdict on a programme, presented as a type of rotation.
explanation.definitionFit: A telemark is a skiing turn with one ski advanced and the knee bent, named after a Norwegian region.

clue.text: Dangerously losing head in a flippant manner

indicators.note: losing head means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: hairy is slang for dangerous, so hairily means dangerously

explanation.surface: Someone recklessly beheaded while acting carelessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hairy' as slang for dangerous is the hard step; 'losing head' removes H.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking airily is being light-hearted and offhand, a synonym for flippantly.

clue.text: Desire of traveller with tiny amount of money, first to last

indicators.note: first to last says the opening letter moves to the end

parts.note: titchy is British slang for tiny
a fee is an amount of money charged

explanation.surface: A traveller who longs to roam with only a pittance in their pocket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first to last' moves the T from the front of TITCHYFEE to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Having itchy feet is an idiom for restlessness and the urge to travel.

clue.text: Man penning very short fictional work

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so the man holds the short letter

parts.note: Noel is a man's name
v is the short form of very

explanation.surface: A man writing a brief piece of fiction.
explanation.definitionFit: A novel is a book-length piece of prose fiction.

clue.text: Entertainment award makes old poet hug maiden repeatedly

indicators.note: hug means wrap around, so the poet encloses the letters

parts.note: Thomas Gray, eighteenth-century poet of the Elegy

indicators.note: repeatedly means the letter appears twice

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A trophy ceremony where an old poet keeps embracing a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: The Grammy is the American music industry's annual award.

clue.text: Generous UK politician of yesteryear?

definitions.meaning: a member of the old ... Party, merged in 1988 into the ... Democrats

explanation.surface: A bountiful statesman from bygone days.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberal means giving freely, and the Liberals were a major British party until 1988.

clue.text: Get back to find maiden maybe by sports ground

parts.note: rec is short for recreation ground
a maiden is one kind of over in cricket, six balls without a run

explanation.surface: Recovering a lost item found near a playing field.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden in cricket is an over with no runs scored.
explanation.definitionFit: To recover something is to regain or retrieve it.

clue.text: Endless despondency faced by one in hut in cold place

indicators.note: faced by means the numeral stands in front

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: endless means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: gloom is despondency

explanation.surface: Someone sits miserable and alone in an Arctic shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' trims the last letter and 'faced by' puts the numeral first; 'cold place' belongs to the definition, not the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An igloo is a dome-shaped Inuit shelter built of snow blocks in polar regions.

clue.text: Language that can equally well be written right to left

definitions.note: the clue's only definition word also stands as the whole wordplay, since this tongue's name is a palindrome

indicators.text: that can equally well be written right to left
indicators.note: says the word reads the same in either direction

parts.note: the clue's only definition word also stands as the whole wordplay, since this tongue's name is a palindrome

explanation.surface: A tongue whose name is symmetrical, as a puzzle about writing direction.
explanation.walkthrough: Some scripts run right to left, which tempts a solver toward Arabic or Hebrew.
explanation.definitionFit: Malayalam is a Dravidian tongue spoken in Kerala, southern India.

clue.text: Dirty vehicle of the French belts around

parts.note: du is French for of the

indicators.note: around says the word for belts is turned round

parts.note: tracts are belts or stretches of land

explanation.surface: A grimy French car with straps fastened about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' is the reversal signal; 'Dirty vehicle' reads as a description but is the definition, of a British bin lorry.
explanation.definitionFit: A dustcart is a British rubbish lorry, a vehicle that is often filthy.

clue.text: Clergy in church when keeping free from fancy stuff

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as he left'
plain means unadorned

explanation.surface: Ministers in a church that shuns ornament.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaplains are clergy attached to institutions such as hospitals or regiments.

clue.text: Make out first of soldiers entering to attack

indicators.note: entering puts that letter inside the word for attack

parts.note: to decry is to criticise or attack

indicators.note: first of takes the opening letter of soldiers

explanation.surface: Spotting the lead troops moving in to assault.
explanation.definitionFit: To descry is to catch sight of, to discern something distant.

clue.text: To grumble I deem silly — live for the moment

parts.note: to carp is to grumble

indicators.note: silly suggests the letters of 'I deem' are scrambled

explanation.surface: A complainer calls a carefree attitude foolish.
explanation.definitionFit: Carpe diem is Latin for seize the day, a motto for enjoying the present.

clue.text: Weird child, terror not half unruly

indicators.note: unruly says the letters run wild into a new order
not half keeps only the first half of terror

explanation.surface: A strange little one, half a holy terror and badly behaved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half' keeps TER from TERROR; 'unruly' rearranges CHILD + TER.
explanation.definitionFit: Eldritch is a Scots-origin word meaning eerie or unearthly.

clue.text: Plan once more presented in colour (green)

parts.note: red is a colour
green can mean raw, inexperienced

explanation.surface: A design submitted again, this time coloured green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'green' looks like the colour, but it means inexperienced.
explanation.definitionFit: To redraw a design is to draft it afresh, to plan it again.

clue.text: Precise cooking without this ultimately? Maybe, maybe not

definitions.text: Precise cooking without this ultimately? Maybe, maybe not

indicators.note: cooking means the letters of precise are worked into a new mix
ultimately takes the last letter of this

explanation.surface: Can you cook accurately without written instructions? Perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: PRECISE minus S (last of 'this') rearranges to the answer; 'without' marks the removal. The whole clue also asks whether exact cooking needs one.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of instructions for a dish is what precise cooking may or may not depend on.

clue.text: Old writer in another world almost and cunning with it

indicators.note: almost drops the final letter

parts.note: Pluto is another world in the solar system
arch means knowing or sly

explanation.surface: A classical author who lived in his own sly fantasy.
explanation.definitionFit: Plutarch was a Greek biographer of the first and second centuries.

clue.text: Emperor had managed to capture island

indicators.note: to capture means to hold inside

parts.note: ran means managed, as in ran a business

explanation.surface: A ruler who conquered an isle.
explanation.definitionFit: Hadrian was the Roman emperor famed for his wall across northern England.

clue.text: A trio's excited to find spiritual enlightenment

indicators.note: excited means stirred up, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Three seekers thrilled to reach a mystical awakening.
explanation.definitionFit: Satori is the Zen Buddhist term for sudden awakening.

clue.text: Fabric this person put in a line to stuff into seat

indicators.note: to stuff into means to push inside

parts.note: a chair is a seat

indicators.note: put in places the setter inside a and the line letter

parts.note: this person is the setter, me

explanation.surface: Someone upholsters a chair, padding it with material.
explanation.walkthrough: Two nested insertions: 'put in' makes AMEL, and 'to stuff into' places that inside the seat. Collins prints the fabric as one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Camelhair is cloth woven from the soft hair of camels, used for coats.

clue.text: Motorway with sign of no movement — one's got stuck

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main north–south motorway, the 1 read as I
a red traffic light signals stop

explanation.surface: Stuck in a jam on the motorway at a stop signal.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 runs from London to Leeds; read the 1 as I.
explanation.definitionFit: To be mired is to be bogged down, trapped as in a swamp.

clue.text: Animal will get caught retreating — that's what one believes

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards

parts.note: a deer is an animal
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A beast running back from capture, framed as a statement of faith.
explanation.definitionFit: A creed is a set of beliefs or principles.

clue.text: Island captured by revolutionary female leader

indicators.note: captured by means held inside

parts.note: Che Guevara, the Argentine-born revolutionary

explanation.surface: An island seized by a rebel woman who leads them.
explanation.definitionFit: A chief is a head or person in command.

clue.text: One firm behind left entrance

indicators.note: behind places those letters after the word for left

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
I is the Roman numeral for one
Co is short for company

explanation.surface: A company that left a doorway behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: A portico is a porch with columns at a building's front door.

clue.text: Capital city is built anew, one having displaced university

indicators.note: anew means made again, so the letters are reassembled
having displaced means one letter pushes out another

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A capital rebuilt after a university was moved out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having displaced' swaps U in IS BUILT for I, giving ISBIILT; 'anew' rearranges that.
explanation.definitionFit: Tbilisi is the capital of Georgia in the Caucasus.

clue.text: I'm on hand with stuff to be put out for actor

indicators.note: to be put out means disturbed, so the letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: A stagehand ready to clear props out of the way.
explanation.definitionFit: Dustin Hoffman is an American film star of The Graduate and Rain Man.
